Uruk-Iraq.name: Uruk
Uruk-Iraq.evidence_basis: Twin Kullaba-Eanna Ubaid settlements (~15 ha) coalescing into ~70 ha Early Uruk, ~140 ha Middle Uruk and ~230-250 ha Late Uruk metropolis (~90-100 inh/ha, Adams & Nissen 1972; Finkbeiner 1991; Algaze 2008).

Tell Brak-Syria.name: Tell Brak
Tell Brak-Syria.evidence_basis: Khabur Basin centre expanding from ~5 ha Halaf-Ubaid mound to ~55 ha LC2 (~4000 BC) and ~130 ha indigenous LC3-4 proto-urban metropolis with corona of outer mounds (~100 inh/ha, Ur, Karsgaard & Oates 2007, 2011).

Susa-Iran.name: Susa
Susa-Iran.evidence_basis: Founded ~4200 BC as ~15 ha Susa I ceremonial terrace and necropolis, surging to ~50-60 ha Susa II/Proto-Elamite urban capital (~140 inh/ha, Hole 1987; Potts 2016).

Hamoukar-Syria.name: Hamoukar
Hamoukar-Syria.evidence_basis: Northeastern Syrian ~15 ha walled citadel plus sprawling low-density Southern Extension (~280 ha obsidian-working zone; Ur 2010; Gibson et al. 2002), contracting after the ~3500 BC siege destruction.

Hierakonpolis-Egypt.name: Hierakonpolis
Hierakonpolis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Largest Predynastic Upper Egyptian proto-city expanding across ~55-60 ha of wadi-and-floodplain residential quarters, breweries and HK29A ceremonial precinct (~105-115 inh/ha, Hoffman 1982; Friedman 2011; Kemp 2006).

Nippur-Iraq.name: Nippur
Nippur-Iraq.evidence_basis: Central alluvial Euphrates centre growing from ~7 ha Ubaid village to ~38-42 ha Late Uruk proto-city (~115-125 inh/ha built density, Adams 1981; Gibson 1992).

Eridu-Iraq.name: Eridu
Eridu-Iraq.evidence_basis: Southernmost Sumerian lagoon temple-town expanding from ~10-12 ha Ubaid 1-4 ceremonial centre (Levels XVII-VI) to ~38 ha Late Uruk urban node (~120 inh/ha, Safar, Mustafa & Lloyd 1981; Adams 1981).

Catalhoyuk-Turkey.name: Catalhoyuk
Catalhoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Konya Plain East Mound (~13.5 ha of contiguous honeycombed mudbrick houses; Cessford 2005 and Hodder 2014 model ~3,500-5,500 at -6500) transitioning to smaller Chalcolithic West Mound (~4 ha) after -6000.

Naqada-Egypt.name: Naqada
Naqada-Egypt.evidence_basis: Upper Egyptian Predynastic walled regional capital growing from ~10 ha Naqada I village to ~33 ha Naqada II-III South Town and cemeteries (~125 inh/ha, Hassan 1988; Kemp 2006).

Ur-Iraq.name: Ur
Ur-Iraq.evidence_basis: Lower Euphrates marsh-edge settlement expanding from ~8-10 ha Ubaid village (Woolley 1955) to ~30 ha Late Uruk proto-city (~125 inh/ha, Wright 1981).

Tell Abu Hureyra-Syria.name: Tell Abu Hureyra
Tell Abu Hureyra-Syria.evidence_basis: Euphrates terrace tell growing from ~0.5 ha Natufian hamlet (~135 inh) to ~11.5-16 ha LPPNB megasite (~3,500-4,500 inh peak in Moore, Hillman & Legge 2000) before Pottery Neolithic contraction.

Ain Ghazal-Jordan.name: Ain Ghazal
Ain Ghazal-Jordan.evidence_basis: Expands from ~4.5 ha in MPPNB to ~13-15 ha LPPNB megasite (~190-210 inh/ha contemporaneous occupancy, Rollefson & Kohler-Rollefson 1989; Kuijt 2000; Birch-Chapman 2017) before PPNC and Yarmoukian contraction.

Chogha Mish-Iran.name: Chogha Mish
Chogha Mish-Iran.evidence_basis: Susiana Plain ~18 ha regional centre from Archaic Susiana through Protoliterate Uruk horizon (~135 inh/ha at peak before partial shift toward Susa, Delougaz & Kantor 1996; Alizadeh 2008).

Shahr-i Sokhta-Iran.name: Shahr-i Sokhta
Shahr-i Sokhta-Iran.evidence_basis: Helmand Delta urban foundation at ~3200 BC (Period I) spanning ~15-20 ha of planned mudbrick quarters and craft areas (~140 inh/ha, Tosi 1983; Sajjadi 2014).

Tepe Sialk-Iran.name: Tepe Sialk
Tepe Sialk-Iran.evidence_basis: Kashan oasis ~3.5 ha North Mound Neolithic village expanding to ~14 ha South Mound Sialk III-IV silver-and-copper metallurgical and Proto-Elamite town (~165 inh/ha, Ghirshman 1938; Shahmirzadi 2004).

Tepe Hissar-Iran.name: Tepe Hissar
Tepe Hissar-Iran.evidence_basis: Damghan Plain copper-smelting and lapis-trade town expanding from ~8 ha Hissar I to ~14 ha Hissar II (~160 inh/ha, Schmidt 1937; Dyson & Howard 1989).

Village of the Pyramid Builders (Heit el.name: Village of the Pyramid Builders (Heit el-Ghurab

Buto-Egypt.name: Buto
Buto-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northwestern Nile Delta settlement expanding from ~6 ha Maadi-Buto fishing-farming mound to ~18 ha Naqada III mudbrick administrative town (~120 inh/ha, von der Way 1997; Hartung et al. 2009).

Basta-Jordan.name: Basta
Basta-Jordan.evidence_basis: Southern Jordanian LPPNB terraced megasite spanning ~10-14 ha of dense multi-room limestone-built structures (~175-200 inh/ha contemporaneous built area, Nissen et al. 2004; Gebel et al. 2006).

Kadhima Areas ABC, E, F and G-Kuwait.name: Kadhima Areas ABC, E, F and G

Teleilat Ghassul-Jordan.name: Teleilat Ghassul
Teleilat Ghassul-Jordan.evidence_basis: Ghassulian Chalcolithic type-site spanning ~20 ha of clustered mudbrick broadroom compounds and sanctuary precinct northeast of the Dead Sea (~90 inh/ha overall footprint, Bourke 2007).

Domuztepe-Turkey.name: Domuztepe
Domuztepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Kahramanmaras ~20 ha Late Halaf mega-village with dense tholoi, rectangular complexes and communal ritual ditch; excavators estimate ~1,500-2,000 inhabitants (Campbell et al. 1999; Carter et al. 2003).

Arslantepe-Turkey.name: Arslantepe
Arslantepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Malatya Plain ~4.5 ha mound expanding from Period VIII-VII Ubaid-Late Chalcolithic centre into Period VIA monumental palatial complex with surrounding residential town (Frangipane 2012).

Mundigak-Afghanistan.name: Mundigak
Mundigak-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Kandahar Plain Helmand-culture mound growing from ~2.0 ha Period I semi-sedentary village to ~6 ha Period II and ~12 ha Period III proto-urban mudbrick centre (~140 inh/ha, Casal 1961; Shaffer 1978).

Ras Shamra-Syria.name: Ras Shamra
Ras Shamra-Syria.evidence_basis: Northern Levantine tell expanding from ~2.0 ha Level VC aceramic village through Level IV Halaf and Level IIIB Ubaid-Chalcolithic to ~7.5 ha (~190 inh/ha, Contenson 1992).

Sha'ar HaGolan-Israel.name: Sha'ar HaGolan
Sha'ar HaGolan-Israel.evidence_basis: Yarmoukian Pottery Neolithic type-site spanning ~20 ha of large courtyard houses separated by planned streets (~70 inh/ha dispersed village density, Garfinkel & Miller 2002).

Byblos-Lebanon.name: Byblos
Byblos-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Levantine coastal promontory growing from ~1.2 ha Early Neolithic lime-plastered monocellular houses to ~5.0 ha Late Chalcolithic/EB I nucleated town (~250 inh/ha, Dunand 1973; Garfinkel 2004).

Maadi-Egypt.name: Maadi
Maadi-Egypt.evidence_basis: Lower Egyptian Predynastic ~15 ha trade and copper-working village (~6 ha active core of oval posts-and-matting huts and subterranean Levantine-style dwellings, Rizkana & Seeher 1989; Hartung 2014).

Mersin-Yumuktepe-Turkey.name: Mersin-Yumuktepe
Mersin-Yumuktepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Cilician coastal ~4.5 ha stratified tell from Early Neolithic through Level XVI fortified Chalcolithic citadel (~240-260 inh/ha at Chalcolithic peak, Caneva & Koroglu 2010).

Tepe Gawra-Iraq.name: Tepe Gawra
Tepe Gawra-Iraq.evidence_basis: Assyrian piedmont ~2.0 ha elite acropolis plus surrounding lower settlement evolving from Halaf/Ubaid tripartite temples (Level XIII) to Late Chalcolithic craft-administrative town (Tobler 1950; Rothman 2002).

Jericho-Palestine.name: Jericho
Jericho-Palestine.evidence_basis: Excavated tell area grows from ~2.5 ha in PPNA (walled enclosure and stone tower, Kenyon 1981; Kuijt 2000) to ~4.0 ha in MPPNB (~220-270 inh/ha, Birch-Chapman 2017), contracting sharply in Pottery Neolithic before Early Bronze IA regrowth.

Merimde Beni Salama-Egypt.name: Merimde Beni Salama
Merimde Beni Salama-Egypt.evidence_basis: Western Delta margin ~25 ha shifting Neolithic village (~5-6 ha occupied simultaneously with oval mud-clod huts and basket granaries, ~180 inh/ha active zone, Eiwanger 1984-1992; Kemp 2006).

Asikli Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Asikli Hoyuk
Asikli Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Cappadocian ~4.0 ha Aceramic Neolithic densely agglomerated mudbrick settlement along the Melendiz River (~245 inh/ha built density, Ozbasaran et al. 2018).

Tol-e Nurabad-Iran.name: Tol-e Nurabad
Tol-e Nurabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Mamasani Valley ~9.0 ha multi-period mound with ~2-6 ha contemporaneously occupied core from Mushki/Jari Neolithic through Lapui and Early Banesh (~160 inh/ha, Potts et al. 2009).

Yanik Tepe-Iran.name: Yanik Tepe
Yanik Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: Lake Urmia Basin ~4.5 ha tell progressing from Late Neolithic and Chalcolithic strata into dense circular-house Early Transcaucasian/Kura-Araxes town (~210 inh/ha, Burney 1961; Summers 2013).

Choga Mami-Iraq.name: Choga Mami
Choga Mami-Iraq.evidence_basis: Mandali piedmont ~5.5 ha Samarra-to-Transitional village with earliest attested gravity-flow irrigation canals and buttressed multi-room houses (~160 inh/ha, Oates 1969, 2013).

Tell Halaf-Syria.name: Tell Halaf
Tell Halaf-Syria.evidence_basis: Upper Khabur Halaf culture type-site covering ~5.5 ha of painted-pottery residential strata beneath the later Iron Age tell (~155 inh/ha, Oppenheim 1943; Becker 2013).

Tepe Yahya-Iran.name: Tepe Yahya
Tepe Yahya-Iran.evidence_basis: Soghun Valley ~3.0 ha mound spanning Periods VII-IVC from Chalcolithic farming hamlet to Proto-Elamite administrative-craft outpost (~220-260 inh/ha compact tell, Lamberg-Karlovsky & Beale 1986; Potts 2001).

Cayonu-Turkey.name: Cayonu
Cayonu-Turkey.evidence_basis: Ergani Plain ~3.8 ha Upper Tigris Aceramic Neolithic village evolving from round huts through grill-plan and cell-plan stone-founded houses (~205 inh/ha peak, Ozdogan 1999).

Ovcular Tepesi-Azerbaijan.name: Ovcular Tepesi
Ovcular Tepesi-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Nakhchivan Arpa Valley ~10 ha terraced hill settlement (~3.5-4.5 ha contemporaneous Late Chalcolithic and early Kura-Araxes copper-working core, ~160 inh/ha, Marro et al. 2011, 2019).

Tepe Zagheh-Iran.name: Tepe Zagheh
Tepe Zagheh-Iran.evidence_basis: Qazvin Plain ~4.0 ha Transitional Chalcolithic planned mudbrick village with painted ritual building (~170 inh/ha peak, Negahban 1979; Fazeli Nashli et al. 2009).

Kissonerga-Mosphilia-Cyprus.name: Kissonerga-Mosphilia
Kissonerga-Mosphilia-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Western Cypriot ~12 ha dispersed Late Neolithic to Middle Chalcolithic regional centre of circular lime-plastered buildings (~55-60 inh/ha dispersed footprint, Peltenburg 1998).

Sang-e Chakhmaq-Iran.name: Sang-e Chakhmaq
Sang-e Chakhmaq-Iran.evidence_basis: Shahroud Plain dual-mound site: ~0.8 ha aceramic West Mound transitioning to ~4.5 ha ceramic East Mound with plastered rectangular dwellings (~150 inh/ha, Masuda 1974; Roustaei et al. 2015).

Gobekli Tepe-Turkey.name: Gobekli Tepe
Gobekli Tepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Upper Mesopotamian ~9.0 ha PPNA-EPPNB ridge settlement combining monumental T-pillar enclosures with newly excavated domestic quarters and cisterns (~60-75 inh/ha resident core, Clare 2020; Dietrich et al. 2019).

Tell Sabi Abyad-Syria.name: Tell Sabi Abyad
Tell Sabi Abyad-Syria.evidence_basis: Balikh Valley ~4.5 ha multi-mound Late Neolithic and Halaf settlement featuring the Burnt Village storehouses and administrative sealings (~140 inh/ha, Akkermans 1996, 2014).

Tal-i Iblis-Iran.name: Tal-i Iblis
Tal-i Iblis-Iran.evidence_basis: Bardsir Valley ~2.8 ha Chalcolithic tell (Periods 0-V) with extensive crucible copper-smelting workshops (~190-210 inh/ha peak, Caldwell 1967; Frame 2012).

Ulucak Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Ulucak Hoyuk
Ulucak Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Aegean Anatolian ~3.0 ha Early Neolithic farming tell east of Izmir with dense rectangular pise and mudbrick dwellings (~180 inh/ha at Level IV, Cilingiroglu et al. 2012).

Mureybet-Syria.name: Mureybet
Mureybet-Syria.evidence_basis: Middle Euphrates ~2.8 ha Natufian-to-EPPNB tell with multicellular round houses and communal structures (~175 inh/ha at Phase III-IV peak, Cauvin 1977; Ibanez 2008).

Tell Oueili-Iraq.name: Tell Oueili
Tell Oueili-Iraq.evidence_basis: Earliest excavated southern Mesopotamian alluvial village (~3.5 ha Ubaid 0-4) featuring monumental tripartite houses and cellular granaries (~140 inh/ha, Huot 1991, 1996).

Aougni N'ait Ourigh Neolithic Site. C-13.name: Aougni N'ait Ourigh Neolithic Site. C-1300 (Oukaïmeden

Hacilar-Turkey.name: Hacilar
Hacilar-Turkey.evidence_basis: Southwestern Anatolian Lakes District ~1.8 ha mound progressing from Aceramic levels to Level VI-II fortified mudbrick village (~250 inh/ha peak, Mellaart 1970; Duru 2008).

Khirokitia-Cyprus.name: Khirokitia
Khirokitia-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Walled Aceramic Neolithic ~3.0 ha hilltop village of tightly packed circular stone-and-mudbrick houses; Le Brun (1984, 2001) estimates ~300-600 concurrent inhabitants.

Tall-e Bakun-Iran.name: Tall-e Bakun
Tall-e Bakun-Iran.evidence_basis: Marvdasht Plain ~2.2 ha Bakun B2-A craft and administrative village yielding >140 clay door-and-bale sealings (~195 inh/ha, Alizadeh 2006).

Ilipinar-Turkey.name: Ilipinar
Ilipinar-Turkey.evidence_basis: Marmara ~2.5 ha spring-fed village featuring planned concentric rows of mudbrick houses in Phases VI-VB (~170 inh/ha, Roodenberg 2008).

Mentesh Tepe-Azerbaijan.name: Mentesh Tepe
Mentesh Tepe-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Middle Kura ~1.8 ha multi-period settlement spanning Shulaveri-Shomu Neolithic, Sioni/Leilatepe Chalcolithic and Early Kura-Araxes (~160-210 inh/ha, Lyonnet et al. 2016).

Tell Hassuna-Iraq.name: Tell Hassuna
Tell Hassuna-Iraq.evidence_basis: Northern Mesopotamian ~2.0 ha Hassuna culture type-site south of Mosul with courtyard-centred mudbrick farmsteads and granaries (~170 inh/ha, Lloyd & Safar 1945).

Goytepe-Azerbaijan.name: Goytepe
Goytepe-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Middle Kura Basin ~2.0 ha circular-compound Neolithic tell (~145 m diameter), largest excavated Shulaveri-Shomu mound (~170 inh/ha, Nishiaki & Guliyev 2020).

Said Qala Tepe-Afghanistan.name: Said Qala Tepe
Said Qala Tepe-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Arghandab Valley ~1.8 ha Chalcolithic tell (Periods I-III) featuring mudbrick compound architecture and Quetta-style painted wares (~190 inh/ha, Shaffer 1978).

El-Badari-Egypt.name: El-Badari
El-Badari-Egypt.evidence_basis: Middle Egyptian ~2.2 ha Badarian-Amratian low-desert spur villages and stratified Hemamieh settlement (~140 inh/ha, Brunton & Caton-Thompson 1928; Holmes & Friedman 1994).

Jerf el-Ahmar-Syria.name: Jerf el-Ahmar
Jerf el-Ahmar-Syria.evidence_basis: Twin-mound ~1.5 ha PPNA Middle Euphrates village organized around subterranean communal granary-meeting buildings EA30 and EA53 (~175 inh/ha, Stordeur 2015).

Nemrik 9-Iraq.name: Nemrik 9
Nemrik 9-Iraq.evidence_basis: Upper Tigris ~1.8 ha PPNA-EPPNB terrace village with multi-pillar semi-subterranean mud-plastered round houses (~150 inh/ha peak, Kozlowski 2002).

Kortik Tepe-Turkey.name: Kortik Tepe
Kortik Tepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: Upper Tigris ~1.5 ha Younger Dryas-PPNA sedentary hunter-fisher mound with dense circular dwellings and >450 sub-floor burials (~165 inh/ha peak, Ozkaya & Coskun 2011; Benz et al. 2015).

Deh Morasi Ghundai-Afghanistan.name: Deh Morasi Ghundai
Deh Morasi Ghundai-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Kandahar Plain ~1.2 ha Chalcolithic farming tell (Periods I-II) with multi-room mudbrick houses and household shrine contemporary with Mundigak III (~200 inh/ha, Dupree 1963).

Kom W-Egypt.name: Kom W
Kom W-Egypt.evidence_basis: Fayum Neolithic ~2.0 ha lakeside hearth-mound settlement associated with Upper K basket-lined cereal granary silos (~120 inh/ha, Caton-Thompson & Gardner 1934; Wendrich et al. 2010).

Beidha-Jordan.name: Beidha
Beidha-Jordan.evidence_basis: Excavated ~0.5 ha PPNB corridor-house village in southern Jordan; micro-level Bayesian building-use and sleeping-space modelling by Birch-Chapman et al. (2017) and Byrd (2005) yields ~120-240 concurrent inhabitants.

Dosariyah-Saudi Arabia.name: Dosariyah
Dosariyah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Largest Arabian Neolithic and Ubaid-contact coastal site in Eastern Arabia spanning ~2.5 ha of stratified shell middens, plaster floors and posthole dwellings (~95 inh/ha, Masry 1974; Drechsler 2018).

Gardan Reg-Afghanistan.name: Gardan Reg
Gardan Reg-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Lower Helmand/Sistan desert-margin ~1.5 ha Chalcolithic settlement and copper-slag craft cluster surveyed by Fairservis (1961) and Dales (1972) (~150 inh/ha).

Ra's al-Hamra-Oman.name: Ra's al-Hamra
Ra's al-Hamra-Oman.evidence_basis: Muscat coastal headland ~1.2 ha fishing-and-mangrove shell-midden villages (RH-6 and RH-5) with semicircular posthole huts and >200 burials (~165 inh/ha, Biagi & Nisbet 2006; Salvatori 2007).

Ali Kosh-Iran.name: Ali Kosh
Ali Kosh-Iran.evidence_basis: Deh Luran Plain ~1.3 ha mound spanning Bus Mordeh, Ali Kosh and Mohammad Jaffar phases; Hole, Flannery & Neely (1969) directly estimate ~100-200 inhabitants.

Dakhla Oasis-Egypt.name: Dakhla Oasis
Dakhla Oasis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Mid-Holocene Bashendi oasis settlement clusters featuring >50 slab-built circular hut foundations and hearth mounds (~150-200 aggregate oasis villagers, McDonald 2009, 2016).

Shulaveris Gora-Georgia.name: Shulaveris Gora
Shulaveris Gora-Georgia.evidence_basis: Kvemo Kartli ~1.1 ha Shulaveri-Shomu Neolithic type-site with tightly clustered circular mudbrick dwellings and storage silos (~170 inh/ha, Kiguradze 1986; Hamon et al. 2016).

Wadi Faynan 16-Jordan.name: Wadi Faynan 16
Wadi Faynan 16-Jordan.evidence_basis: Excavated ~0.6-0.8 ha PPNA settlement of semi-subterranean pise structures clustered around communal amphitheatre O75 (~220 inh/ha built zone, Finlayson & Mithen 2007; Mithen et al. 2018).

Jarmo-Iraq.name: Jarmo
Jarmo-Iraq.evidence_basis: Zagros piedmont ~1.3 ha aceramic-to-ceramic village in Chemchemal Valley; ~20-25 contemporaneous tauf mudbrick houses support ~150-180 inhabitants (Braidwood et al. 1983).

Ayios Epiktitos-Vrysi-Cyprus.name: Ayios Epiktitos-Vrysi
Ayios Epiktitos-Vrysi-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Northern Cypriot coastal headland ~1.0 ha Ceramic Neolithic village of tightly packed sunken rectilinear mudbrick houses (~175 inh/ha, Peltenburg 1982).

Aknashen-Armenia.name: Aknashen
Aknashen-Armenia.evidence_basis: Ararat Plain ~0.8 ha circular Neolithic mound (~100 m diameter) with dense pise and mudbrick round buildings (~190 inh/ha, Badalyan et al. 2010, 2022).

Al-Sihi-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Sihi
Al-Sihi-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Southern Tihama Red Sea littoral ~1.0 ha coastal shell-midden village participating in trans-Red Sea obsidian exchange networks (~145 inh/ha, Zarins & Al-Badr 1986; Khalidi 2009).

Wisad Pools-Jordan.name: Wisad Pools
Wisad Pools-Jordan.evidence_basis: Eastern Jordanian Black Desert basalt-hut pastoral aggregation beside seasonal wadi pools (>300 stone structures with ~20-30 concurrent huts, Rollefson et al. 2014, 2018).

Medjez II-Algeria.name: Medjez II
Medjez II-Algeria.evidence_basis: Setif High Plains ~0.8 ha giant Upper Capsian rammadiya (escargotiere) mound with >3.5 m stratified habitation ash deposits (~165 inh/ha seasonal aggregation, Camps-Fabrer 1975; Merzoug et al. 2016).

Al-Buhais 18-United Arab Emirates.name: Al-Buhais 18
Al-Buhais 18-United Arab Emirates.evidence_basis: Sharjah piedmont seasonal pastoralist aggregation and cemetery containing >500 individuals buried over several centuries (~115-130 group size, Uerpmann et al. 2006, 2013).

Jubabat al-Juruf-Yemen.name: Jubabat al-Juruf
Jubabat al-Juruf-Yemen.evidence_basis: Dhamar highland ~0.8 ha early terrace-farming village yielding earliest radiocarbon-dated domesticated emmer wheat, barley and lentils in southwest Arabia (~160 inh/ha, Ekstrom & Edens 2003; Wilkinson 2005).

Haua Fteah-Libya.name: Haua Fteah
Haua Fteah-Libya.evidence_basis: Jebel Akhdar Cyrenaica ~0.5 ha monumental karstic cave and forecourt spanning Libyco-Capsian foragers and Neolithic caprine herders from ~5500 BC (McBurney 1967; Barker et al. 2009, 2010).

Al-Ula Neolithic-Saudi Arabia.name: Al-Ula Neolithic
Al-Ula Neolithic-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Northwestern Arabian volcanic plateau clusters of 4-8 m double-walled standing stone circle dwellings linked to mustatil pastoral ritual landscapes (Dalton et al. 2024; Thomas et al. 2021).

As-Sabiyah-Kuwait.name: As-Sabiyah
As-Sabiyah-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Kuwait Bay ~0.6 ha Ubaid-contact maritime village with stone-walled cellular chambers, bitumen-coated reed boat fragments and pearl diving (~120 residents, Carter & Crawford 2010).

El-Mekta-Tunisia.name: El-Mekta
El-Mekta-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Gafsa Basin ~0.6 ha Capsian culture type-site rammadiya with dense lithic workshops and snail-shell middens (Gobert 1952; Rahmani 2004; Mulazzani et al. 2016).

Suwayh-Oman.name: Suwayh
Suwayh-Oman.evidence_basis: Ja'alan Arabian Sea ~0.7 ha coastal lagoon shell-midden hamlet specialized in marine fishing and shell-ring manufacture (~140 inh/ha, Charpentier et al. 2003).

Jebel Oraf-Saudi Arabia.name: Jebel Oraf
Jebel Oraf-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Southern Nefud palaeolake shoreline hearth arrays (~170 hearths) documenting seasonal Holocene cattle-pastoralist aggregations (~70-95 people, Guagnin et al. 2017, 2020).

Tashkurgan 40-Afghanistan.name: Tashkurgan 40
Tashkurgan 40-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Bactrian alluvial-fan ~0.8 ha Kelteminar-affiliated Neolithic open-air settlement mapped by Soviet-Afghan surveys (~115 inh/ha, Vinogradov 1979).

Ifri Oudadane-Morocco.name: Ifri Oudadane
Ifri Oudadane-Morocco.evidence_basis: Eastern Rif coastal rockshelter and terrace (~0.3 ha) transitioning from Epipalaeolithic foragers to Early Cardial Neolithic farmers with domestic wheat, barley and legumes by ~5600 BC (Linstadter & Kehl 2012; Morales et al. 2013).

Takarkori-Libya.name: Takarkori
Takarkori-Libya.evidence_basis: Tadrart Acacus ~0.4 ha rockshelter and wadi-terrace camp preserving stone hut foundations, wild-grain processing pottery and dairy-pastoralist burials before late Holocene aridification (Biagetti & di Lernia 2013; Dunne et al. 2012).

Klimonas-Cyprus.name: Klimonas
Klimonas-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Earliest Cypriot PPNA farming hamlet spanning ~0.5 ha of round earth-built dwellings around a 10 m communal building (~180 inh/ha, Vigne et al. 2012, 2023).

Gueldaman-Algeria.name: Gueldaman
Gueldaman-Algeria.evidence_basis: Soummam Valley ~0.4 ha karstic cave and hillside settlement documenting intensive Neolithic caprine pastoralism and impressed pottery from ~5000-2800 BC (Kherbouche et al. 2014, 2016).

Siwa Oasis-Egypt.name: Siwa Oasis
Siwa Oasis-Egypt.evidence_basis: Northwestern Desert depression ~0.6 ha Early-to-Mid Holocene lacustrine Epipalaeolithic and Neolithic camps around palaeolake Shiata (Hassan & Gross 1987).

Aq Kupruk-Afghanistan.name: Aq Kupruk
Aq Kupruk-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Balkh River valley ~0.35 ha rockshelter and river-terrace complex spanning Kuprukian Epipalaeolithic to Aceramic and Ceramic Neolithic with early domesticated sheep/goat (Dupree 1972; Davis 1978).

Kehf el-Baroud-Morocco.name: Kehf el-Baroud
Kehf el-Baroud-Morocco.evidence_basis: Atlantic Moroccan ~0.4 ha Late Neolithic-Chalcolithic cave and open-air pastoral-agricultural community dated ~3700 BC (Mikdad et al. 2000; Fregel et al. 2018).

Columnata-Algeria.name: Columnata
Columnata-Algeria.evidence_basis: Tiaret plateau ~0.5 ha stratified Columnatian-Capsian to Early Neolithic open-air shell-midden settlement and necropolis (Cadenat 1966; Sari 2014).

Hassi Mouillah-Algeria.name: Hassi Mouillah
Hassi Mouillah-Algeria.evidence_basis: Northern Algerian Bas-Sahara ~0.6 ha sebkha-margin Neolithic habitation with ostrich-eggshell beads, ceramics and bifacial points (Marmier & Trecolle 1972; Aumassip 1986).

Shakshuk-Libya.name: Shakshuk
Shakshuk-Libya.evidence_basis: Western Jebel Gharbi/Jefara spring-fed ~0.5 ha Epipalaeolithic and Neolithic settlement cluster mapped by the Italian-Libyan Mission (Barich & Garcea 2008; Barich et al. 2010).

Eynan-Israel.name: Eynan
Eynan-Israel.evidence_basis: Late and Final Natufian sedentary hamlet covering ~0.25 ha of stone-walled semi-subterranean dwellings beside Lake Hula (~50-80 concurrent residents, Valla et al. 2007).

Shuwaymis-Saudi Arabia.name: Shuwaymis
Shuwaymis-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Interior Arabian wadi aggregation and rock-art centre evidencing continuous Holocene hunter-herder seasonal occupation during the Arabian Humid Period (Guagnin et al. 2018).

Wadi at-Tayyilah 3-Yemen.name: Wadi at-Tayyilah 3
Wadi at-Tayyilah 3-Yemen.evidence_basis: Khawlan highland ~0.4 ha aceramic Neolithic pastoralist hamlet of elliptical stone-built dwellings associated with early cattle herding (Fedele 2008, 2013).

Izriten-Morocco.name: Izriten
Izriten-Morocco.evidence_basis: Tarfaya Atlantic littoral ~0.4 ha stratified coastal dune shell-midden and burial settlement spanning Epipalaeolithic through Neolithic (Grebenart 1975; Onrubia-Pintado 1988).

Darra-i Kur-Afghanistan.name: Darra-i Kur
Darra-i Kur-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Badakhshan ~0.3 ha Mountain Neolithic shelter and valley camp yielding Goat Cult pit burials, black-burnished pottery and microliths (Dupree 1972).

Amekni-Algeria.name: Amekni
Amekni-Algeria.evidence_basis: Hoggar massif ~0.4 ha granite-shelter and wadi-bank Early Neolithic camp with wavy-line ceramics and wild-millet grinding equipment (Camps 1969).

Oued Chebeika-Morocco.name: Oued Chebeika
Oued Chebeika-Morocco.evidence_basis: Southern Moroccan Atlantic coast ~0.4 ha Holocene marine-mollusc midden and pastoralist camp along relict wadi terraces (Vernet 2007; Saenz de Buruaga 2014).

Kef Zoura D-Algeria.name: Kef Zoura D
Kef Zoura D-Algeria.evidence_basis: Telidjene Basin ~0.3 ha stratified Typical-to-Upper Capsian rockshelter and talus midden (~50-65 residents, Lubell et al. 2009; Jackes & Lubell 2014).

Tin Hanakaten-Algeria.name: Tin Hanakaten
Tin Hanakaten-Algeria.evidence_basis: Tassili n'Ajjer ~0.3 ha deeply stratified Epipalaeolithic to Pastoral Neolithic shelter with hut floors, pottery and burials near Djanet (Aumassip 1984; Roubet 2001).

Manayzah-Yemen.name: Manayzah
Manayzah-Yemen.evidence_basis: Wadi Sana Hadramawt stratified rockshelter and open-air pastoralist camp (~0.3 ha) documenting fluted arrowheads and early domesticates (Crassard et al. 2006; McCorriston & Martin 2009).

Abiar Miggi-Libya.name: Abiar Miggi
Abiar Miggi-Libya.evidence_basis: Eastern Jebel Gharbi ~0.3 ha Neolithic of Capsian Tradition rockshelter and plateau camp yielding impressed pottery and bifacial arrowheads (Neuville 1956; Barich 2014).

Tifariti-Western Sahara.name: Tifariti
Tifariti-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Northern Western Sahara ~0.5 ha humid-phase wadi-basin occupation and pastoral aggregation mapped by the Western Sahara Project (Clarke & Brooks 2018).

Uan Afuda-Libya.name: Uan Afuda
Uan Afuda-Libya.evidence_basis: Wadi Teshuinat ~0.25 ha Early and Late Acacus hunter-gatherer cave documenting penned wild Barbary sheep dung horizons and basketry (di Lernia 1999).

Ashash-Western Sahara.name: Ashash
Ashash-Western Sahara.evidence_basis: Zemmour interior ~0.25 ha stratified rockshelter excavated by Borrell et al. (2015) with AMS-dated 9th-millennium BP microliths and mid-7th-millennium BP early pottery.
